event.what_happened: The Nasdaq Composite fell 11.2% between 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-20, 5.28% of it on the last day. Press reports tie the fall to doubts about whether enthusiasm for AI had peaked, slower data-center expansion and higher borrowing costs. That link is reported, not confirmed. Separately, the Federal Reserve says the buildout is increasingly funded by debt.
event.how_it_reaches_markets: Large index weight of AI-linked companies; debt used to fund data centers; possible regulatory opposition to data center construction.

sourced_facts.text: Federal Reserve Governor Barr, 2026-11-16: 'the AI buildout has been increasingly funded by debt'; on-balance-sheet debt of the seven largest AI firms 'is expected to exceed $800 billion before year's end'; he adds that he is 'less concerned about direct losses' given the still-limited debt behind the boom

Federal Reserve Financial Stability Report (November 2026, data to 2026-10-28): 'Bond issuance by the largest investment-grade firms involved in operating data centers was greater than $150 billion year to date'; 'Measures of equity valuations have remained elevated since the previous report'
Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,466.19 on 2026-11-11, 24,429.88 on 2026-11-18 and 22,617.73 on 2026-11-20 (down 5.28% that day), then 24,129.50 on 2026-11-27 (FRED series NASDAQCOM)

Governor Barr, same speech: 'Anyone watching the news or their retirement plans these past couple of weeks is aware of the questions that investors have raised about the sustainability of the AI investment boom'

history.note: Card opened. Resolution conditions written before the outcome is known.

Title was 'Doubts about financing of the AI buildout'. Changed to say only what is confirmed. Conditions and forecasts unchanged.

Sources read again: both Federal Reserve facts match. The Nasdaq level for the first condition is now read: 25,466.19. Title was 'Debt-funded AI buildout (sell-off reported, not confirmed)'; the fall is confirmed from the index series, its link to AI debt is not. The Dell example was moved to unconfirmed. unconfirmed_facts: 2026-11-20: S&P 500 seventh straight decline; -3.70% to 6,910.39; Nvidia about -14%: Fortune (read directly) reports the seventh straight loss but gives -3.59% to 6,918.45, and a market-wrap site gives -3.70% and Nvidia -13.8%. The two disagree and neither is on our list of accepted sources. AMD -13.3% was not found
2026-11-25: Nasdaq 100 briefly 20% below its record closing high: not found in anything we read

Dell beat forecasts on 2026-11-24 and its shares fell about 7% the next day: Dell's release of that date shows record revenue and a higher full-year outlook (read as a repost, not at Dell); the share move was not found

notes: 'The day before the losing streak began' is read as 2026-11-11, the last close before the S&P 500's seven straight declines that press reports say ended on 2026-11-20. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,466.19 that day (FRED series NASDAQCOM, read 2026-11-28). The Nasdaq itself rose on 2026-11-18, so its own unbroken run of declines began from 24,429.88; the higher level is used because it is harder to meet.
'Largest AI infrastructure spenders' means Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle. 'Large AI-linked borrower' means one with at least $1 billion of debt outstanding.

items.measure: Nasdaq Composite closes above 25,466.19 (its close on 2026-11-11) on 20 trading days in a row
VIX closes below 20 on 20 trading days in a row (this is what 'Moderate or lower' means under rule v3)
At least 2 of 5 companies (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Oracle) state capital spending guidance equal to or above their previous guidance in a quarterly report released after 2026-11-26
items.latest: 0 of 2. No quarterly report from the five since the card opened

items.measure: A borrower with at least $1 billion of debt misses a payment or cancels an announced financing: 1 case is enough
Any one of the five companies lowers its stated capital spending guidance

counter_view.text: The debt behind the buildout is still small next to the cash these companies earn: a Federal Reserve governor said he is 'less concerned about direct losses'. A fall in share prices is not a failed financing, and no borrower has missed a payment.

worsened_when_any: A large AI-linked borrower misses a debt payment or cancels a publicly announced financing
A major AI infrastructure spender publicly cuts its capital spending plan

readings.en: S&P 500 fall from its one-year high (AFMX record)
